key_insight: Entrance-driven vortices in lab-scale DCMD create Reynolds-number-dependent temperature polarization bias, so module geometry can change both the size and even the sign of the measured effect.
engineering_relevance: Membrane distillation correlations and module comparisons must account for entrance hydrodynamics, because side-chamber length and channel height can systematically distort apparent heat transfer and TP.
method: 3D CFD of direct-contact membrane distillation modules
Swept inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CFD results showing that vortices persist farther downstream as Reynolds number increases and that TP deviation shifts from stronger to weaker relative to a straight-channel baseline across geometries.
watch_item: The conclusions come from simulations of specific lab-scale geometries, so the correction may not transfer directly to other module designs or operating ranges without validation.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
